feedback:
Written before this candidate has raced, so no outcome is stated. The controller is the iteration-6 set (kp 4.8, kd 0.9, ki 0.5, base_speed 1.3, last_direction), which scored 696.6, the best so far. The one change is geometry: sensor footprint 12 mm to 16 mm and the array widened from ±3 cm to ±4 cm at 1.33 cm spacing, with y = 0.06 and seven sensors kept. The limits are respected: sensor x values lie within ±0.08, the footprint is one of the allowed sizes, and the weights stay within ±2. The evidence is iteration 6: oval 20/20 (max_error 0.0095, steering_oscillation 0.232), s-bend 20/20 (progress 0.997, line_loss_events 0.25), and slalom 0/20 (progress 0.47, 1.25 line-loss events per run, off track every run). Slalom is the main lost score, so the coverage hypothesis is worth one clean test. The change is isolated to geometry, so any result can be read against iteration 6.

One point to watch: the weights were kept at ±2 at the outer sensors, but the outer sensors now sit at ±4 cm. The signal slope per centimetre of line offset falls from about 0.67 per cm (±3 cm) to about 0.50 per cm (±4 cm). That is roughly a 25 percent drop in effective steering gain at the same kp, which could cost some oval and s-bend margin even if slalom coverage improves. The weights cannot be scaled up without leaving the ±2 limit, so any compensation has to come through kp.

How to read the next race: if slalom line_loss_events fall clearly (below about 0.8) and oval and s-bend hold, keep this geometry and consider a modest kp increase (for example 5.0) to recover effective gain. If slalom progress rises but oval or s-bend max_error grows or completions drop, the lower effective gain is the cause, so restore it with kp near 5.5 before changing geometry again. If slalom line losses stay at about 1.25 per run, coverage is not the limit and the 16 mm change should be reverted to 12 mm.
requested_changes: If slalom line_loss_events fall clearly below about 0.8 per run and oval and s-bend hold at 20/20 and 20/20, keep geometry at 16 mm and ±4 cm, and try controller.kp 5.0 (kd 1.0) to recover the effective steering gain lost to the wider spacing, since the signal slope fell about 25 percent.

If oval or s-bend completions drop or max_error rises while the sensor span is widened, set controller.kp to about 5.5 with kd 1.0 to restore effective gain at the new spacing, before reverting geometry, since the drop comes from the lower signal slope rather than from coverage.

If slalom line_loss_events stay near 1.25 per run, revert geometry.sensor_size to 0.012 and sensor_positions to ±3 cm, keeping iteration-6 controller values, since coverage is then not the limit and the iteration-6 design remains the best known baseline.
